title: Each tile shows the same figure as its matching report
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
  2. You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  3. You are in a location (workplace) that has invoices and technician clocked time this month (one day is enough) and over the last twelve months.
  4. Your role can create a work order and an invoice in that location (Admin can).

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 3: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: on the Dashboard, Revenue on This Month is above $0.00 and Technician Efficiency on This Month shows a percentage (not -). If not, create today's data first: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save; Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = Tech ShopView, Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; clock time as the technician: in a second browser or a private window, on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Tech (this signs you in as Tech ShopView, a technician at Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 with Time Clock on); open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start; when done click Stop > Clock Out; to make the time exact, as Admin: the three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (n) > edit the record's start and end (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows); on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice). Then check again. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu and leave every tile on its default range.
  2. Write down the Revenue headline.
  3. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue" (it opens the Sales report on the same range) and read the report's total for the invoices' subtotals at the foot of the table.
  4. Go back to the dashboard, write down the Billing Efficiency headline, then click its arrow icon (Service Advisor Analysis report) and read the report's overall figure with all advisors selected.
  5. Go back, write down the Technician Efficiency headline, then click its arrow icon (Technician Efficiency report, Invoiced) and read the overall figure with all technicians selected.
  6. Go back, write down the Technician Utilization headline, then click its arrow icon (Technician Utilization report) and read the overall figure with all technicians selected.
  7. Go back, write down the Sales by Customer headline, then click its arrow icon (Sales By Customer report) and read how many customers the report lists in total (e.g. the pager reads "1 - 10 of 69").
  8. Create one new invoice in the same location today: Work Orders > Create Work Order > a customer and asset > Save; in New Line add a labor line (e.g. Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO, $100 an hour, Estimated Time 1) and tick Line Approved > Save & Close; Story > Update; Complete; Mark Reviewed; Finance > Create Invoice.
  9. Within one minute, reload the dashboard and read the Revenue headline.
  10. Reload the Sales report on the same range and read its total.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Revenue equals the Sales report total exactly, to the cent.
  • Billing Efficiency equals the Service Advisor Analysis figure, Technician Efficiency equals the Technician Efficiency report figure, and Technician Utilization equals the Technician Utilization report figure, each to two decimal places.
  • Sales by Customer equals the number of customers the Sales By Customer report lists (e.g. 69 customers and "1 - 10 of 69").
  • Straight after the new invoice, both the tile and the report have gone up by the same amount (e.g. $100.00) and still agree. There is no wait, and the tile never shows an older figure than the report.
  • If any tile and its report disagree at any point, the case fails. Write both figures in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas and Report Parity); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 3. Report links per the Story 10 context note.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S3-N1: “If a measure's report shows a value, the matching tile shows the same value; the two never disagree.”
  • S3 context note (parity check): “to check parity on a KPI tile that shows a shop-wide figure, compare it against the matching report with all advisors or all technicians selected (no filter applied).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
